content.intended_use: Identify the derivative computed by the fixed-lambda Forward-HG recurrence.

proofs.full_local_argument: Local reconstruction, separate from the source text: Write J_t=D_lambda s_t. Since s_0 is constant, J_0=0. Finite composition of the smooth Phi_t makes s_t differentiable for every t. Applying the chain rule to lambda↦(s_{t-1}(lambda),lambda)↦Phi_t(s_{t-1}(lambda),lambda) gives J_t=A_t J_{t-1}+B_t. Thus J_0=Z_0, and if J_{t-1}=Z_{t-1} the identical recurrence yields J_t=Z_t, proving equality for all t by induction. To expand, define P_{r,t}=A_r A_{r-1} ... A_{t+1} for 1≤t<r and P_{r,r}=I_d. For r=1, Z_1=B_1=sum_{t=1}^1 P_{1,t}B_t. If Z_{r-1}=sum_{t=1}^{r-1}P_{r-1,t}B_t, multiplying by A_r on the left and adding B_r gives Z_r=sum_{t=1}^{r-1}P_{r,t}B_t+P_{r,r}B_r. Induction proves the expansion at r=T. Finally the chain rule for f=E∘s_T gives D_lambda f=∇E(s_T)J_T=∇E(s_T)Z_T and substitution gives the stated sum. Every product has shape d×d, every propagated term d×m, and the final row has shape 1×m.

assumptions: Each Phi_t is smooth as stipulated in Section 2; E is continuously differentiable. All maps are defined on the stated spaces, so all finite iterates and derivatives exist.
s_0 is constant with respect to lambda; E has no direct lambda argument. The maps, T and lambda are fixed during differentiation.
statement.conclusion: With Z_0=0_{d×m} and Z_t=A_t Z_{t-1}+B_t, one has Z_t=D_lambda s_t for every t=0,...,T. Hence D_lambda f(lambda)=∇E(s_T)Z_T=∇E(s_T) sum_{t=1}^T (A_T A_{T-1} ... A_{t+1})B_t. The t=T product is I_d; matrix order is exactly as displayed. This is the selected Forward-HG output.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For positive integers d,m,T, let lambda∈R^m and s_0∈R^d be fixed independently of lambda. Define s_t(lambda)=Phi_t(s_{t-1}(lambda),lambda), t=1,...,T, and f(lambda)=E(s_T(lambda)). Phi_t:R^d×R^m→R^d and E:R^d→R. Set A_t=D_s Phi_t(s_{t-1}(lambda),lambda)∈R^{d×d}, B_t=D_lambda Phi_t(s_{t-1}(lambda),lambda)∈R^{d×m}; gradients of scalar functions are rows.
statement.parameter_domains: d,m,T∈{1,2,...}; s_0∈R^d; lambda∈R^m. No step-size, convexity, contraction, minimizer or asymptotic regime is assumed.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such d,m,T,s_0,Phi_1,...,Phi_T,E and every lambda∈R^m, the identity holds pointwise. No expectation or random-sampling guarantee is asserted.
